Rashi on Eruvin 102a:10:1.hebrew: עשה לו בית יד - לנגר שאינו קשור כלל, ותחב בית יד באמצעיתו, ודומה למקבת, דהשתא ודאי מוכח מילתא הוא דכלי הוא — מהו לנעול בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:10:1.english: [If] one made a handle for it - For a bolt that is not tied at all, and he inserted a handle into its middle, and it resembles a mallet, so that now it is certainly evident that it is a utensil — what is [the halakha regarding] locking with it?

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:10:2.hebrew: בוכנא קאמרת - הא ודאי שרי. בוכנא — מקבת, וכותשין בו חטין ותבלין:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:10:2.english: You are speaking of a pestle - That is certainly permitted. A pestle [is] a mallet, and they pound wheat and spices with it:

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:11:1.hebrew: שריתא - קורה, כמו "בצל קורתי" (בראשית י״ט:ח׳) — "בטלל שרותי":
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:11:1.english: A beam - A beam, as in: “Under the shadow of my roof beam [korati]” (Genesis 19:8) — [rendered by Onkelos as:] “In the shadow of my beam [sherutei]”.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:11:2.hebrew: בי עשרה - כלומר, משאוי עשרה בני אדם היה בה, ואפילו הכי לא אסר עלייהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:11:2.english: A group of ten - That is to say, it was a load for ten people, and even so, he did not forbid [it] to them.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:11:3.english: And they would place it against the door - To support it [the door] at night.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:11:4.english: The status of a utensil - For it is fit to sit upon.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:12:1.english: A mortar - [In Old French:] mortier [meaning a mortar].

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:12:2.hebrew: אדריבא - לתך חטין, ט"ו סאין, חצי כור:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:12:2.english: An adriva - A letekh of wheat, [which is] fifteen se’ah, half a kor.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:13:1.hebrew: כיפי דארבא - אולמות שעושין בספינה, שנועצין כעין מעגלין שקורין צרק"ל — ראשו אחד בדופן זה של ספינה וראשו שני בדופן זה, והוא כפוף כמו אולם ועומד כמו כיפה, ומרחיק כחצי אמה ונועץ אחר, וכן על פני כולה, ופורסין בגדים ומחצלות של גמי להגין מפני הצנה והגשמים: (*):(*)
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:13:1.english: The arches of a boat - [These are] vaulted canopies that they make in a boat, where they insert circular [rods], which are called cercles [hoops] — one of its ends in this side of the boat and its other end in that side, and it is bent like a vault and stands like an arch. And one moves about half a cubit away and inserts another, and likewise across the entire [length of the boat], and they spread garments and reed mats [over them] to protect against the cold and the rains. (*):(*)

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:13:2.hebrew: שיש בהם טפח - שרוחב של מעגל טפח, דבציר מטפח לא הוי אהל, אבל כשרוחב טפח מקרי אהל. נמצא שם אהל עליו מבעוד יום, וכשהוא פורס עליו הבגד למחר — אינו אלא מוסיף:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:13:2.english: When they are a handbreadth [wide] - That the width of the hoop is a handbreadth, for [anything] less than a handbreadth is not a tent, but when its width is a handbreadth, it is called a tent. [Thus,] the status of a tent is upon it from while it was still day, and when he spreads the cloth over it on the morrow, he is merely adding [to an existing tent].

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:13:3.english: Or even if there is not a handbreadth in its width, and there are not three [handbreadths] between this one and that one - For one can say [that the principle of] lavud [applies].

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:15:2.english: That during the day required shade - Because of the heat.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:15:3.hebrew: ובליליא בעו אוירא - הנאת הקור מפני הבל הקיץ. ובימות החול היו פורסין עליהן מחצלות ביום ונוטלין בלילה:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:15:3.english: And at night they required air - The benefit of coolness, because of the heat of summer. And on weekdays, they would spread mats over them by day and remove [them] at night.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:15:4.english: He came before Rav - [To ask:] What shall we do for them on Shabbat?

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:16:1.hebrew: כרוך בודיא - כשתסתלק המחצלת מעליהן לפנות ערב שבת, אל תסלקנה כולה משם, אלא הוי גולל אותה וכורך מעל הגג, ושייר בה טפח פרוסה, דלהוי עליה שם אהל:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:16:1.english: Roll up the mat - When the mat is removed from upon them towards the eve of Shabbat, do not remove it entirely from there; rather, roll it up and wind it over the roof, and leave a handbreadth of it spread out, so that the status of a tent remains upon it.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:16:2.english: And on the following day unroll it - For it is an addition [to an existing tent], and is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:17:1.english: A curtain - [Hung] in front of the doorway for privacy.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:17:2.hebrew: מותר לנטותו - דלאו אהל הוא, דלא קביעא התם, אלא כן דרכו לינתן ולהסתלק, כדלת בעלמא:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:17:2.english: One is permitted to spread it out - For it is not a tent, as it is not fixed there [permanently]; rather, such is its manner: to be put up and taken down, like an ordinary door.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:18:1.hebrew: כילת חתנים - לאו אהל הוא, מפני שאין לה גג למעלה רוחב טפח, מפני שהיא נתונה בשיפוע. והיא יריעה שפורסין סביב למטה לישן:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:18:1.english: A bridal canopy - It is not [considered] a tent, because it does not have a roof at the top a handbreadth wide, as it is positioned at an incline. And it is a curtain that one spreads around the bed to sleep [in].

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:19:1.hebrew: שאין בפחות משלשה סמוך לגג טפח - שנתונה באלכסון קצר, שכשאתה מודד רחבה למטה משלשה לגגה — אין בו רוחב טפח, דהוי כוליה דופן ואין כאן אהל כלל. אבל הרחיבה עד טפח בתוך שלשה לגגה — כאילו גגה טפח דמי, ואסור לנטותה: (*):(*)
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:19:1.english: That [its width] is not a handbreadth within three [handbreadths] of the top - That it is set at a steep incline, so that when you measure its width within three [handbreadths] below its top, it does not have a width of a handbreadth, for the whole thing is [considered] a wall, and there is no tent here at all. But if it widened to a handbreadth within three [handbreadths] of its top, it is considered as though its top is a handbreadth [wide], and it is prohibited to spread it: (*):(*)

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:1:1.hebrew: כשאין ניטל באיגדו - שהחבל דק, ואם היה רוצה ליטלו משם לטלטלו ע"י אותו חבל, מיד נפסק. ר"א סבר: כיון דאינו ניטל באיגדו, דהוה כמי שאינו קשור; ותנן לקמן: נגר המונח שאינו קשור בדלת אין נועלין בו, והאי נמי מונח הוא — משום גלוסטרא לא שרי ליה. ורבי יוסי סבר: גלוסטרא מהניא ליה, דכיון דכלי הוא, לא הוי כבנין:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:1:1.english: When it cannot be picked up by its cord - For the cord is thin, and if one wanted to pick it up from there to move it by means of that cord, it would immediately snap. Rabbi Eliezer holds: Since it cannot be picked up by its cord, it is considered as though it is not tied [at all]; and we learned later: A loose bolt that is not tied to the door, one may not lock [a door] with it, and this [bolt] is also [considered] loose — [and] on account of the knob, [Rabbi Eliezer] does not permit it. But Rabbi Yosei holds: The knob is effective for it, for since it is a vessel, [using it] is not [considered] like building.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:2:1.hebrew: נגר הנגרר - שקשור בדלת, אבל אינו תלוי, שהחבל ארוך; ומתוך שנגרר, אינו נראה כקשור. וכשאין בראשו גלוסטרא קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:2:1.english: A bolt that drags - [One] that is tied to the door, but is not suspended, as the rope is long; and since it drags, it does not appear tied. And [the Mishnah] is speaking [of a case] where there is no knob on its head.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:2:2.hebrew: נועלין בו במקדש - דשבות בעלמא הוא, דאינו בונה ממש, הואיל וקשור לכך; אלא, הואיל ונגרר — מיחזי כבונה. ואין שבות דרבנן במקדש, דלא גזרו שם:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:2:2.english: One may lock [a door] with it in the Temple - For it is merely a rabbinic prohibition [shevut], as it is not actual building, since it is tied for this [purpose]; rather, since it drags, it appears like building. And there is no rabbinic prohibition in the Temple, for they did not issue decrees there.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:3:1.hebrew: והמונח - שאינו קשור כלל, הוי בנין ממש. ור' יהודה סבר: לאו בנין ממש הוא, אלא דומה לבנין, ובמקדש לא גזרו שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:3:1.english: And one that rests - Which is not tied at all — it is actual building. And Rabbi Yehuda maintains: It is not actual building, but rather resembles building, and in the Temple they did not decree a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:4:1.hebrew: זה אפי' במדינה מותר - הואיל וקשור, אף על פי שאינו תלוי:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:4:1.english: This is permitted even in the country - Since it is tied, even though it is not suspended.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:5:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יהודה בנגרר - דמותר אפילו במדינה. אבל לא במונח — דשרי ליה רבי יהודה במקדש — לית הלכתא כוותיה, דכיון שאינו קשור, שם בנין גמור הוא, כשאר נגרים שנועצים בכותלים, והבונה כל שהוא חייב, ומלאכה דאורייתא לא הותרה במקדש חוץ מהקרבת תמידין ומוספין וקרבנות צבור שדוחין את השבת מגזירת הכתוב:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:5:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda regarding a dragged bolt - That it is permitted even in the province outside the Temple. But not with regard to a resting bolt, which Rabbi Yehuda permits in the Temple — the halakha is not in accordance with him. For since it is not tied, it has the status of full construction, like other bolts that are driven into walls, and one who builds any amount is liable; and labor prohibited by Torah law was not permitted in the Temple, except for the offering of daily offerings, additional offerings, and communal offerings, which override Shabbat by biblical decree.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:6:1.hebrew: והוא שקשור בדלת - עצמה, דמוכח שפיר, ולא שקשור במזוזה:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:6:1.english: And that is if it is tied to the door - [To the door] itself, for it is clearly evident [that it belongs to the door], and not that it is tied to the doorpost.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:6:2.hebrew: ניטל באיגדו - כלומר, קשור היה בחבל חזק:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:6:2.english: [It could be] lifted by its cord - That is to say, it was tied with a strong rope:

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:7:1.hebrew: דין לא נטרוק - זה לא ינעול, שאינו קשור, דכמאן דליתיה לגמי דמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:7:1.english: This one shall not lock - This [person] shall not lock [with it], because it is not [considered] tied, for the reed is regarded as if it does not exist.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:8:1.hebrew: נקמז מהו - שנכנס הנגר בחור האסקופה, ונפחת אותו החור, ויוצא הנגר לצד הקרקע ונועץ בקרקע. ועד השתא איירי כשהאסקופה גבוהה, ואין החור ניקב עד לארץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:8:1.english: [If] it was pressed [into the ground], what is [the halakha]? - Where the bolt enters the hole in the threshold, and that hole became broken through, and the bolt emerges toward the ground and is stuck into the ground. And until now, [the Gemara] was dealing with [a case] where the threshold is high and the hole was not perforated through to the ground.

Rashi on Eruvin 102a:8:2.hebrew: נשמט - שנפסק החבל שהוא קשור בו, והרי הוא מונח בקרן זוית כשפותח אותו:
Rashi on Eruvin 102a:8:2.english: Was detached - That the cord to which it is tied was severed, and behold, it lies in a corner when he opens [the door]:

Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:11:1.hebrew: ההוא שריתא דהוו מדלו לה בי עשרה - ואם תאמר: דאמרינן סוף במה מדליקין (שבת דף לה.) גבי חלתא, אמר אביי: "בעי מיניה דמר, אפילו בת תרי כורי — ולא שרי לי"? ויש לומר: דלא דמי; דחלתא אין רגילות לטלטלה בחול כלל, אבל האי שריתא — דרכה לטלטלה תמיד בחול לנעול הדלת, משום הכי שרי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:11:1.english: "A certain beam that ten [people] would lift" - And if you say: But we say at the end of [the chapter] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 35a) regarding a large basket [chalta]: Abaye said, "I asked the Master, [and] even [for one] of two kor he did not permit [it] for me"? And one can say: [The cases] are not comparable, for a large basket is not customarily moved during the week at all, but this beam — its ordinary use is to be moved regularly during the week to lock the door; because of this, it is permitted.

Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:18:1.hebrew: לא אמרן אלא שאין בשיפועה טפח - פירש בקונטרס: שיש כילות קטנות סמוכות זו לזו, ואין בכל אחת טפח. ותימה: דלימא לבוד מכילה זו לכילה זו, ונמצא שיש בשיפועה טפח! ויש לומר: דהא דחשיב ליה אהל לעיל על ידי לבוד — דהיינו לענין שיוכל להוסיף למחר בשבת; אבל לא מסתבר שיחשב בכי האי גוונא עשיית אהל, לאסור עליו לעשות בשבת, דאטו יהיה אסור לנטות בשבת שני חוטין תוך שלשה משום עשיית אהל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:18:1.english: "We said [this] only where its slope does not have a handbreadth" - Rashi explained that there are small canopies adjacent to one another, and in none of them is there a handbreadth [of slope]. And this is astonishing: for let us say [the principle of] lavud [applies] from this canopy to that canopy, and it will turn out that its slope has a handbreadth! And one can say: That which [the Gemara] earlier considered a tent by means of lavud, that was regarding being able to add [to it] the next day, on Shabbat; but it is not reasonable that in such a case it should be considered making a tent, so as to prohibit him from making it on Shabbat — for would it really be prohibited to spread two cords on Shabbat within three [handbreadths of each other] on account of making a tent?!

Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:5:1.hebrew: הלכה כר"י בנגרר - פירש בקונטרס: דנועלין בו במדינה, אבל במאי דשרי מונח במקדש — לית הלכתא כוותיה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:5:1.english: "The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda with regard to [a bolt] that is dragged" - The kuntres [Rashi] explained that one may lock with it in the provinces, but regarding that which [Rabbi Yehuda] permitted [a bolt that is] resting in the Temple, the halakha is not in accordance with him.

Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:8:1.hebrew: נקמז מהו - פירוש: עד השתא הוה איירי כשהאסקופה גבוהה, ואין החור נוקב עד לארץ; והשתא בעי: אם החור הולך עד שנכנס ונועץ בקרקע, ודמי טפי לבונה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 102a:8:1.english: "If it was pressed, what is [the halakha]" - Explanation: Until now, [the Gemara] was dealing with [a case where] the threshold is high and the hole does not pierce through to the ground; and now [Rabbi Zeira] asks: What if the hole extends until [the bolt] enters and is stuck into the ground, and [thus] it more closely resembles building?
